$comment: Ten questions, one per culture axis plus a reversed check on c_direction.
Single-item axes are ACCEPTABLE here, unlike in the belief instrument. Self-report on working
style is direct, someone knows whether they want to be in an office, where belief elicitation
needs several items to denoise. c_direction keeps two items as the acquiescence check.
The skip control matters MORE here than in the belief quiz, not less. A newcomer who has never
held a research job genuinely does not know whether they want mentorship or autonomy. 'It
depends' is a real answer that enters the average; 'I have never worked anywhere so I cannot
say' is a skip and must drop the item. The skip is labelled in those words rather than
generically, because this is the population the product exists for and the failure mode is a
newcomer inventing preferences to finish the form.

questions.text: I'd rather be handed a well-defined problem than choose what to work on.
I get restless when someone else sets the direction of my work.
I do my best work alone or in a pair rather than as part of a large project team.
I'd rather ship something rough this month than something careful next year.
It matters to me that my work is public and citable.
I want substantial mentorship rather than to be left to run.
I'd rather join a place with a clear institutional position I share than one where colleagues disagree openly.
I'd be more comfortable somewhere informal than somewhere professional and institutional.
I want to work in person with colleagues most days.
I want colleagues who are part of this community socially, not only professionally.

scale.label: How much does this sound like you?
scale.midpoint_note: "It depends" is an answer and enters the average. "I don't know yet" removes the question, they are different, and the difference matters most for people who have not worked in the field before.

abstain.label: I don't know yet
abstain.help: Removes this question from your profile. Pick it if you have not worked somewhere that would tell you, that is a real answer, and guessing would be worse.
